items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Ruth Brown, whom I’m working with now

ctx.x: What kind of people did you play behind?

Ivory Joe, what’s his name, Ivory Joe Hunter; Ruth Brown, whom I’m working with now; Lavern Baker; The Coasters; The Drifters maybe — no The Drifters; I remember that terrible record “White Christmas” that was so popular.

items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: you mentioned some of the people you played with — Ruth Brown

ctx.x: It was liable to be the same orchestra. Yes. And well the rock ‘n roll groups also were liable to have the same people, it was a slightly different cast, but I learned that the more things one could do, the more gigs you’d be called on, so I could change hats, all of us could really, and start being funky and play for Atlantic Records in the evening, and do Kostelanetz in the morning and somebody else in-between.

That’s so cool. Let’s talk about this. Because I went back and was reading your first interview actually and you mentioned some of the people you played with — Ruth Brown and the Coasters and the Drifters. And you made a comment about their version of “White Christmas.”
Oh yeah. That was a session we did “White Christmas” — was that the Drifters or the Coasters? © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
